description: EAGLE 9.6 editor commands NAME through ROUTEMULTI from the built-in help (alphabetical command reference): naming, schematic nets and breakouts, persistent groups, library editing (PACKAGE, PAD, PIN, PREFIX, pad/pin arrays), PASTE and design reuse, polygons, printing, quick-route and interactive routing, ratsnest, ripup, replace and rotate. Commands are typed in the editor command line, assigned to keys (ASSIGN) or collected in .scr scripts; in the syntax, capital words are keywords, lowercase words are values, | separates alternatives, .. means repeatable and • stands for a mouse click, which is written as a coordinate (x y) in the current GRID unit in scripts.

tools.name: NAME
tools.description: Shows or changes the name of an object in the schematic, board or library editor (in the library: pads, smds, pins and gates). Parts, elements, pads, smds, pins and gates can be addressed by their name even when they are outside the visible area; nets, busses and signals have to be clicked. Use it to replace automatically generated names such as N$1, E$1, S$1 or P$1 with meaningful ones.
tools.usage:
NAME •..
NAME new_name •
NAME old_name new_name

parameters.name: new_name
parameters.description: New name. Letters are converted to upper case; blanks and ';' are not allowed, and ':' is not allowed for nets, parts, module instances, signals and elements because it is reserved for hierarchical names (e.g. AMP1:IC1).

parameters.name: old_name
parameters.description: Existing name of a part, element, pad, smd, pin or gate to rename without clicking it.

tools.notes: When a net or bus consists of several segments a popup asks for This segment (T), Every segment on this sheet (E) or All segments on all sheets (A); in scripts the answer can be preselected with SET CONFIRM OPTn (the SET help shows SET CONFIRM OPT2 followed by NAME GND (x y)). A checkbox (on by default when no label exists) starts LABEL after renaming a net or bus. Renaming a signal polygon asks whether only the polygon (moving it to another signal) or the whole signal is renamed; the eaglerc parameters Cmd.Name.RenameEntireNetByDefault and Cmd.Name.RenameEntireSignalByDefault change the defaults. The main schematic and every module have separate name spaces. Automatic part names come from PREFIX. Related: LABEL, SHOW, REPOSITION, VALUE.

tools.name: NET
tools.description: Draws net wires on the Net layer of a schematic to connect pins: the first click starts the net, each further click ends a segment, and two clicks on the same point finish it. Net ends snap to pin tips within SNAP_LENGTH, a net ends automatically when it hits another net, bus or pin, and a junction is set where it meets at least two other nets/pins. Nets with the same name on different sheets are electrically connected.
tools.usage:
NET [net_name] • [curve | @radius] •..
NET BREAKOUT [PIN | UNIQUE] [LENGTH=VALUE] • •..
NET BREAKOUT [AUTOINCR] [LENGTH=VALUE] net_name • •..

parameters.name: net_name
parameters.description: Name for the new net; without it EAGLE assigns N$n. If the net starts on a bus, a popup offers the bus signals (and part busses) and the net takes that name.

parameters.name: curve | @radius
parameters.description: Draws an arc as part of the net, as described for LINE.

parameters.name: BREAKOUT
parameters.description: Creates labeled breakout nets from clicked pins (see the NET BREAKOUT entry).

tools.notes: Mouse: Right changes the wire bend style (SET WIRE_BEND), Shift+Right reverses the switching direction, Ctrl+Right toggles between corresponding bend styles. SET AUTO_END_NET OFF and SET AUTO_JUNCTION OFF disable automatic ending and junctions (also in Options/Set/Misc). Do not use ',' or '[' ']' in net names (bus syntax: bus D[0..15] contains nets D0..D15). A leading '!' draws the name overlined (active low, see TEXT). Display width: SET NET_WIRE_WIDTH (default 6 mil). Related: BUS, BREAKOUTBUS, PINBREAKOUT, CLASS, NAME, LABEL, JUNCTION.

tools.name: NET BREAKOUT
tools.description: Option of NET that creates short new nets with labels from any pins you click, across any number of schematic parts, so connections can be made by net name instead of drawn wires. The net/label name can be the pin name, a unique part_gate_pin string or a fixed name that can auto-increment. Without further parameters (or via the 'Pin Breakout' button in the NET parameter toolbar) the breakout type is chosen in the user interface.
tools.usage:
NET BREAKOUT [PIN | UNIQUE] [LENGTH=VALUE] • •..
NET BREAKOUT [AUTOINCR] [LENGTH=VALUE] net_name • •..

parameters.name: PIN
parameters.description: Each new net is named after the pin it is connected to.

parameters.name: UNIQUE
parameters.description: Net name is part, gate and pin name concatenated (part_gate_pin).

parameters.name: net_name
parameters.description: Fixed name used for every new net regardless of the pin.

parameters.name: AUTOINCR
parameters.description: Placed before net_name: if the name ends in a digit it increments for each further pin (ADDR1, ADDR2, ADDR3 ...).

parameters.name: LENGTH=VALUE
parameters.description: Minimum length of the new net segments in grid units; the segment is longer if the label text needs more room.

tools.notes: PIN, UNIQUE and AUTOINCR are keywords and cannot be used as net names. Clicks must hit pins. Related: BREAKOUTBUS (break out a bus with labeled nets), PINBREAKOUT (all pins of a part), PINTOBUS.

tools.name: NEWGROUP
tools.description: Creates a persistent, named group from the selected objects that is stored in the design as an object of its own (it may also be empty). A selectable group can be selected and moved, copied, rotated, mirrored or locked as one unit; in a schematic it shows a boundary with a title and is limited to one sheet. A non-selectable group is only a named collection (it can span sheets) and is protected from commands that change the design.

parameters.name: group_name
parameters.description: Name of the new persistent group.
Numeric flag of the syntax; it corresponds to the group's Selectable property described in the help (check the result with INFO on the group, where the flag can be changed).

tools.notes: Ctrl/Cmd+G runs NEWGROUP on the selected objects (shortcut defined in default-assign.scr; the line SCRIPT default-assign.scr in Documents/EAGLE/scripts/eagle.scr must be uncommented). Airwires and attributes cannot be members; objects may belong to several groups, and nested groups are made with EDITGROUP (a selectable group cannot contain a non-selectable one). Non-selectable groups support ATTRIBUTE, DELETE, EDITGROUP, INFO, NAME, SHOW, UNGROUP; selectable groups additionally COPY, LOCK, MIRROR, MOVE, ROTATE. Groups can also be picked in the Design Manager. SET GROUP_ANNOTATIONS controls the schematic annotations.

tools.name: OPEN
tools.description: Opens an existing library for editing, or creates a new library in the first directory of the library path when no library of that name exists. A managed library can be opened by its URN if it has been downloaded and belongs to the current user. Mainly used in scripts; afterwards EDIT loads a symbol, footprint or device of that library.

parameters.name: library_name
parameters.description: Library name (searched in the library path) or file name.

parameters.name: library_urn
parameters.description: URN of a locally available managed library owned by the current user.

tools.notes: OPEN .lbr switches the editor window to the library editor. UNDO/REDO history only reaches back to the last EDIT, OPEN or REMOVE. Related: CLOSE, USE, EDIT, SCRIPT.

tools.name: OPTIMIZE
tools.description: Merges wire segments that lie on one straight line, are on the same layer and have the same width into single wires. This reduces the number of objects and lets a complete track be moved at once. It can act on named signals, nets or busses, on a clicked object, on a group or on the whole drawing.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Signal, net or bus name(s) to optimize.
OPTIMIZE; optimizes all wires of the drawing.

tools.notes: Ctrl+Right optimizes the group (only signal, net or bus wires). Clicking an unnamed wire optimizes all unnamed wires. Optimization runs automatically after MOVE, SPLIT and ROUTE unless SET OPTIMIZING OFF is set or a SPLIT point was clicked twice; the OPTIMIZE command works regardless of that setting.

tools.name: PACKAGE
tools.description: In the device editor of a library, defines, renames, deletes, switches or updates package variants; a variant combines a footprint (and optionally a 3D package) under a variant name that becomes part of the device name. In the schematic or board editor PACKAGE acts exactly like CHANGE PACKAGE. Without parameters a dialog selects footprint, 3D package and variant name; afterwards CONNECT maps pins to pads.
tools.usage:
PACKAGE
PACKAGE pname vname
PACKAGE pname.fpt vname (new in EAGLE 9.1)
PACKAGE pname.pac vname (alternative for backwards compatibility)
PACKAGE pname.p3d vname
PACKAGE urn vname
PACKAGE pname@lname vname
PACKAGE name
PACKAGE -old_name new_name
PACKAGE -name
PACKAGE @vname
PACKAGE @vname pname
PACKAGE @vname pname.pac
PACKAGE @vname pname.3d
PACKAGE @vname urn

parameters.name: pname vname
parameters.description: New variant vname with footprint pname; a 3D package is added automatically if exactly one 3D package in the library references only that footprint.

parameters.name: pname.fpt vname / pname.pac vname
parameters.description: Same, but never adds a 3D package automatically.

parameters.name: pname.p3d vname
parameters.description: Uses a 3D package of the library and creates one variant per footprint of that 3D package.

parameters.name: urn vname
parameters.description: 3D package by URN (form urn:adsk.eagle:package:123/1); it is downloaded and added to the library if missing, one variant per footprint.

parameters.name: pname@lname vname
parameters.description: Fetches footprint pname from library lname and creates the variant (also possible by drag&drop from the Control Panel).

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Switches to an existing variant.

parameters.name: -old_name new_name / -name
parameters.description: Renames or deletes a variant.

parameters.name: @vname [pname | pname.pac | pname.p3d | urn]
parameters.description: Replaces the footprint/3D package of an existing variant while keeping its connections and attributes; @vname alone opens a selection dialog. The replacement must already be in the library.

tools.notes: Device name = device set name + technology + package variant unless the device set name contains '*' (technology) or '?' (replaced by the variant name). Packageless devices are possible for frames, supply devices (one symbol with a Sup pin) and external devices (attribute _EXTERNAL_ assigned in the library); once a package is assigned they are no longer treated that way. A 3D package with more than one footprint cannot be assigned with @vname. Related: CONNECT, TECHNOLOGY, PREFIX, BOARD.

tools.name: PAD
tools.description: Places through-hole pads in a footprint in the library editor: a pad hangs at the cursor and every left click places one. Diameter, shape, orientation, flags and a name can be typed in and stay preset for the following pads. The final shape and diameter on a board are governed by that board's Design Rules.

parameters.name: diameter
parameters.description: Pad diameter in the current unit, up to 200 mm (7.7840 inch).

parameters.name: shape
parameters.description: Square, Round, Octagon, Long (elongated) or Offset (elongated with offset); applies to Top and Bottom only, inner layers are always round. For elongated pads the diameter is the smaller side and the ratio comes from Design Rules Shapes/Elongation (100% = 2:1).

parameters.name: orientation
parameters.description: R0 ... R359.9 (see ADD); the S and M flags are not allowed.

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: NOSTOP (no solder stop mask), NOTHERMALS (no thermals), FIRST (marks the 'first' pad, drawn with the special shape set in the Design Rules; applies only to the next pad).

parameters.name: 'name'
parameters.description: Pad name in single quotes; otherwise names are generated (P$n) and can be changed with NAME.

tools.notes: Right rotates the pad, Shift+Right reverses the rotation direction. Drill size: CHANGE DRILL; shape/diameter later: CHANGE SHAPE / CHANGE DIAMETER. SET DISPLAY_MODE REAL | NODRILL and SET PAD_NAMES OFF | ON affect display. Arbitrary pad shapes: draw a polygon around the pad or wires ending at the pad center in a signal layer (one polygon per pad and layer; extra solder stop must be drawn explicitly; thermals follow the shape). A new PAD command resets flags. A single pad on a board requires a one-pad footprint (vias have no element name and are not in the netlist). Related: SMD, PADARRAY, VIA.

tools.name: PADARRAY
tools.description: Creates a series of pads on one or more sides of a rectangle in the footprint editor in one step, named <base><start> up to <base><start+count-1>. It can also draw a rectangle in tPlace, add >NAME and >VALUE texts and delete existing pads, labels and lines first. From the PAD parameter toolbar icon it opens a dialog; on the command line all arguments must be given.
tools.usage: PADARRAY [sides base start count dx dy unit drawrect includename includevalue deleteobjs]

parameters.name: sides
parameters.description: L, R, LR, T, B or TB (Left, Right, Top, Bottom).

parameters.name: base / start / count
parameters.description: Base name, start index and number of pads.

parameters.name: dx / dy
parameters.description: Distance between pads in X and in Y direction.

parameters.name: unit
parameters.description: MIC, MM, MIL or INCH.

parameters.name: drawrect
parameters.description: ON/OFF: draw a rectangle in the tPlace layer.

parameters.name: includename / includevalue
parameters.description: ON/OFF: place a >NAME / >VALUE text.

parameters.name: deleteobjs
parameters.description: ON/OFF: delete pads, labels and line objects before placing the array.

tools.example: PADARRAY LR P 1 16 7.62 2.54 MM ON ON ON OFF;
tools.notes: The help defines dx/dy only as the X and Y distances between pads; try the dialog once to see how they are applied to the chosen sides. Related: PAD, SMDARRAY, PINARRAY.

tools.name: PASTE
tools.description: Inserts the clipboard contents (made with GROUP and COPY/CUT) into the current drawing, or the complete content of a drawing file or design block. Works in schematics, boards, symbols and footprints but not in the device editor, and only between drawings of the same kind (board to board, schematic to schematic, pads/smds footprint to footprint, pins symbol to symbol). Names that already exist are replaced by new ones.
tools.usage:
PASTE [ orientation ] •
PASTE [ orientation ] [ offset ] filename •
PASTE [ DBL ][ orientation ] [ offset ] filename •

parameters.name: orientation
parameters.description: Rotation/mirroring as in ADD (e.g. R90, MR0).

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Number added to part and net names when pasting from a file (see 'PASTE from a drawing file').

parameters.name: filename
parameters.description: Drawing file to paste; '*' or a directory opens a file dialog; enclose in single quotes if it could be read as orientation or offset.

parameters.name: DBL
parameters.description: Paste a design block (see 'PASTE DBL').

tools.notes: Mouse: Center mirrors, Right rotates, Shift+Right reverses rotation, Ctrl+V pastes the clipboard. Busses keep their names; nets keep them only if a segment has a label or is connected to a supply pin. Modified devices/footprints in the clipboard start an automatic library update; run DRC and ERC afterwards. Files can also be pasted by drag&drop with Ctrl held. In the symbol editor PASTE can create pins from text (see 'PASTE pin list'). Related: CUT, COPY, GROUP.

tools.name: PASTE from a drawing file (design reuse)
tools.description: Pasting a .sch or .brd file inserts its complete content; if the file belongs to a consistent board/schematic pair and such a pair is being edited, both are pasted into the corresponding drawings. An offset is added to all part and net names that do not keep their names, so one circuit can be instantiated several times (e.g. channel 1 at 100, channel 2 at 200). Schematic sheets are appended as new sheets; running the command in the board attaches the pasted board to the cursor for exact placement.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Added to part and net names; without it new names are generated as needed.

parameters.name: filename
parameters.description: Schematic or board file of the block to reuse.

tools.notes: Nets that are labeled or connected to a supply pin (on any sheet) keep their names and connect to existing nets of the same name. Outside scripts a dialog lists all net names so they can be edited. Pasted from the schematic, the board part is placed below the existing board content. Layers, net classes, design rules and autorouter settings of the current drawing are kept (additional layers/classes are added), so restring and clearances may differ from the source: run DRC.

tools.name: PASTE DBL (design block)
tools.description: Pastes a design block, a reusable schematic and/or board fragment saved with WRITE DBL or File > Save selection as Design Block. Without a file name a dialog similar to the ADD dialog opens. Only the parts that match the open editors are pasted: schematic only, board only, or both when a consistent pair is loaded.

parameters.name: DBL
parameters.description: Selects design block mode.

parameters.name: filename
parameters.description: Design block file; omit it to choose in the dialog.

tools.notes: Started in the board editor it behaves like pasting a drawing file: the board is placed by click and schematic sheets are added. Started in the schematic with a one-sheet block, the block is placed by click on the current sheet (no new sheet). Design block files are loaded for preview with EDIT name.dbl. Related: WRITE DBL.

tools.name: PASTE pin list (symbol editor)
tools.description: In the symbol editor PASTE creates pins from comma-, tab- or space-separated text on the clipboard, for example copied from a spreadsheet, text editor or PDF datasheet. A table with a header row naming pin attributes (Name, Length, Function, Direction ...) sets the pin options; missing values use the PIN defaults. Holding Ctrl while starting PASTE switches from single-column to multi-column analysis.
tools.usage: PASTE •   (symbol editor, pin table on the clipboard; hold Ctrl when starting PASTE for multi-column mode)

parameters.name: Name column
parameters.description: Pin names; non-compliant names are fixed (spaces become '_', spaces around '/' are removed, lower case becomes upper case, duplicates become NAME@1, NAME@2 ...).

parameters.name: Length / Function / Direction columns
parameters.description: Values as listed for the PIN command (e.g. Short, Middle, Long; None, Dot, Clk, DotClk; In, Out, Io, Pwr, Sup ...).

tools.example:
Clipboard text:
Name   Length  Function  Direction
VCC    Short   None      Pwr
RESET  Middle  Dot       In
TCK    Middle  DotClk    Io
then in the symbol editor: PASTE (0 0);
tools.notes: To copy one column from a PDF, hold Alt while selecting in a PDF viewer that supports it. Results depend on the source formatting; if it fails, paste into a text editor first and tidy the table.

tools.name: PATTERN
tools.description: Makes several copies of one object and arranges them in a linear pattern (X/Y spacing) or a circular pattern (angle step around a center). Usable in the schematic, layout and library editors. Interactively a dialog asks for the count and spacing; then clicks select the object, the circle center (circular mode) and the position of the first copy.
tools.usage:
PATTERN •..
PATTERN LINEAR item-count x-spacing x-unit y-spacing y-unit object-location first-item-location
PATTERN CIRCULAR item-count degree [ rotate ] object-location circle-center-location first-item-location

parameters.name: item-count
parameters.description: Number of copies.

parameters.name: x-spacing x-unit / y-spacing y-unit
parameters.description: Linear distances between copies with unit INCH, MIL, MM or MIC.

parameters.name: degree
parameters.description: Circular: angle in degrees between two copies.

parameters.name: ROTATE
parameters.description: Circular, optional: rotate each copy along the circle.

parameters.name: object-location / circle-center-location / first-item-location
parameters.description: Coordinates of the object to copy, the circle center and the first copy.

tools.example:
PATTERN LINEAR 5 1.5 INCH 200 MIL (1.5 1.5) (3.0 2.5);
PATTERN CIRCULAR 8 45.0 ROTATE (10 10) (30 30) (40 30);
tools.notes: Right rotates the selected object, Shift+Right reverses the direction. The option table in the help names the rotation keyword 'OPTIONAL', while the syntax line and the help example use ROTATE.

tools.name: PIN
tools.description: Places pins, the connection points for nets, in a symbol in the library symbol editor; the pin is drawn in the Symbols layer and extra information in the Pins layer. Options set the electrical direction (used by ERC and automatic supply wiring), graphic function, length, orientation, name visibility and swap level; they can be given in any order and stay preset for following pins. Pin names must be enclosed in single quotes.

parameters.name: Direction
parameters.description: NC, In, Out (totem-pole), IO, OC (open collector/drain), Hiz (3-state), Pas (passive), Pwr (power input), Sup (supply, e.g. ground symbol). Default IO.

parameters.name: Function
parameters.description: None, Dot (inverter), Clk (clock), DotClk (inverted clock). Default None.

parameters.name: Length
parameters.description: Point (no line, no name), Short (0.1 inch), Middle (0.2 inch), Long (0.3 inch). Default Long.

parameters.name: Orientation
parameters.description: R0 (connection point right), R90 (up), R180 (left), R270 (down). Default R0.

parameters.name: Visible
parameters.description: Off, Pad (pad name only), Pin (pin name only), Both. Default Both.

parameters.name: Swaplevel
parameters.description: Integer; 0 = not swappable, pins with the same number > 0 in a symbol can be swapped with PINSWAP. Default 0.

tools.notes: Starting with a numbered name (PIN 'D0') auto-increments the name for each further click (D1, D2 ...). Right rotates the pin, Shift+Right reverses. Several pins with the same visible name are named GND@1, GND@2 ... (only the part before '@' is shown). Pwr pins are connected automatically to a net with a Sup pin of the same name. Pins cannot be added to or deleted from symbols already used in a device (CONNECT mapping). Name/pad text position and size are fixed. A leading '!' overlines the name. Options can be preset with CHANGE and inspected with SHOW. Related: PINARRAY, PASTE pin list, NAME.

tools.name: PINARRAY
tools.description: Creates a series of pins on the sides of a rectangle in the symbol editor, named <base><start> to <base><start+numpins-1>. Optionally draws a rectangle in the Symbols layer, adds >NAME and >VALUE texts and deletes existing pins, labels and wires first. From the PIN parameter toolbar icon a dialog opens; on the command line all arguments must be given.
tools.usage: PINARRAY [sides base start numpins drawrect includename includevalue deleteobjs]

parameters.name: sides
parameters.description: L, R, T, B or any combination (Left, Right, Top, Bottom).

parameters.name: base / start / numpins
parameters.description: Base name, start index and number of pins.

parameters.name: drawrect
parameters.description: ON/OFF: draw a rectangle in the Symbols layer.

parameters.name: includename / includevalue
parameters.description: ON/OFF: place a >NAME / >VALUE text.

parameters.name: deleteobjs
parameters.description: ON/OFF: delete pins, labels and wires before placing the array.

tools.example: PINARRAY LR IO 0 16 ON ON ON OFF;
tools.notes: Related: PIN, PADARRAY, SMDARRAY.

tools.name: PINBREAKOUT
tools.description: Extends a short net from every pin of a schematic part, optionally named and labeled, so that the part can be connected by net names. It is also available in the right-click context menu of a part.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Name of a part in the schematic.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: 1 = Unique (<part>_<gate>_<pin>), 2 = Pin names (<pin>), 3 = Default (N$1), 4 = None.

tools.notes: Related: NET BREAKOUT (pins of several parts), BREAKOUTBUS, PINTOBUS.

tools.name: PINTOBUS
tools.description: Connects the pins of a schematic part instance to nearby busses with short labeled nets, for every pin whose name is a member of a bus specification. Useful to hook a part onto existing busses without drawing each net. Also available from the part's right-click context menu.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Part instance whose pins are connected.

tools.notes: The busses must be drawn horizontally or vertically and the pins must point towards them. Select the part and all target busses first (Ctrl+Left adds to the selection), otherwise EAGLE asks for them. Related: BUS, PINBREAKOUT, NET BREAKOUT.

tools.name: PINSWAP
tools.description: Swaps two pins of the same symbol that have the same swap level (> 0), or two pads of the same footprint in a board. With forward/back annotation active the pads can only be swapped if their pins are swappable; on a board without schematic the swap level is not checked.

parameters.description: Click the two pins (schematic) or pads (board) to exchange.

tools.notes: Wires attached to swapped pins/pads move with them, so short circuits can result: run DRC afterwards. Swap levels are set with the PIN command. Related: GATESWAP.

tools.name: POLYGON
tools.description: Draws polygon areas. In the signal layers (Top, Bottom, Route2..15) a polygon belongs to a signal and is poured as copper that keeps the clearances from design rules and net classes; in tRestrict, bRestrict and vRestrict it is a keep-out area for the Autorouter; in other layers it is a plain shape. Click the corners and click the start point again (or the same point twice) to close it.

parameters.name: signal_name
parameters.description: Signal the copper polygon belongs to (e.g. GND); enclose names starting with a digit in single quotes ('0V').

parameters.name: width
parameters.description: Line width of the edges, also used for filling; keep it in the range of other wires and above the output device resolution (e.g. not below about 6 mil for a 1 mil Gerber plotter).

parameters.name: curve | @radius
parameters.description: Draws an arc as part of the outline, as described for LINE.

tools.notes: Mouse: Center selects the layer, Right changes the bend style (Shift+Right reverses, Ctrl+Right toggles corresponding styles), Ctrl+Left at a wire end point defines an arc radius. ESC removes the last edge while drawing. Existing polygons are picked at their edges: SPLIT inserts an edge, DELETE removes a corner (with 3 corners left the polygon is deleted), MOVE moves edges/corners, CHANGE LAYER/WIDTH act on the whole polygon, NAME renames the signal. Objects in tRestrict/bRestrict are subtracted from Top/Bottom polygons (e.g. negative text). See also 'POLYGON pour settings' and 'POLYGON outline/real mode, cutouts and _OUTLINES_'. Related: POLYGONIZE, RATSNEST, RIPUP.

tools.name: POLYGON pour settings (Pour, Rank, Thermals, Spacing, Isolate, Orphans)
tools.description: Properties of signal polygons that control the calculated copper; they only matter for polygons in signal layers. Preset them with CHANGE before drawing, apply them to existing polygons with CHANGE and a click, or edit them in the properties dialog.
tools.usage:
CHANGE POUR SOLID | HATCH | CUTOUT •
CHANGE RANK value •
CHANGE THERMALS OFF | ON •
CHANGE SPACING distance •
CHANGE ISOLATE distance •
CHANGE ORPHANS OFF | ON •

parameters.name: Pour
parameters.description: Solid (default), Hatch or Cutout.

parameters.name: Rank
parameters.description: 1..6, default 1. Lower-rank polygons are calculated first and subtracted from higher-rank ones; polygons of the same rank are checked against each other by DRC. Only for signal polygons in a board.

parameters.name: Thermals
parameters.description: On (default) connects pads and smds with thermal spokes; Off connects them solidly. Spoke width: half the pad drill or half the smaller smd side, at least the polygon width, at most twice it.

parameters.name: Spacing
parameters.description: Distance between fill lines for Pour = Hatch (default 50 mil).

parameters.name: Isolate
parameters.description: Clearance to other signals and to Dimension/restrict objects (default 0); the larger of this and the design rule/net class value is used. Leave at 0 unless needed, because larger values can leave gaps to same-signal objects.

parameters.name: Orphans
parameters.description: Off (default) removes isolated copper islands that have no connection to a non-polygon object of the signal; On keeps them.

tools.notes: In hatched polygons, pads, vias and wires can fall through the raster and get airwires; an object counts as connected if a fill or outline line runs through one of its control points. With Orphans Off a polygon can vanish completely; its outlines are then shown on screen but are not printed or output. If a signal consists only of polygons, all parts remain.

tools.name: POLYGON outline/real mode, cutouts and _OUTLINES_
tools.description: Signal polygons are stored and shown as outlines (dotted edges) until RATSNEST calculates them into real mode; RIPUP switches them back to outlines and CHANGE recalculates a polygon already shown in real mode. The CAM Processor always calculates all polygons. A polygon with pour Cutout is subtracted from all other signal polygons in its layer regardless of rank, and the reserved signal name _OUTLINES_ gives a polygon properties used to generate outlines data, e.g. for milling prototype boards.
tools.usage:
RATSNEST;           (calculate polygons, real mode)
RIPUP @;            (all polygons back to outlines)
CHANGE POUR CUTOUT •
POLYGON _OUTLINES_ [width] • • •..

parameters.name: Outlines mode
parameters.description: Default display: only the user-defined outline, drawn dotted.

parameters.name: Real mode
parameters.description: Calculated copper areas as they will be produced.

parameters.name: Cutout
parameters.description: Only in signal layers; outline always dotted; its wire width counts when subtracting and may be very small or zero without inflating CAM data.

tools.notes: The STOP button interrupts calculation (finished polygons stay in real mode). SET POLYGON_RATSNEST OFF stops RATSNEST from calculating polygons. PRINT does not calculate polygons: run RATSNEST before printing. Do not use the name _OUTLINES_ for anything else. The eaglerc parameter Option.DrawUnprocessedPolygonEdgesContinuous draws unprocessed edges as solid lines.

tools.name: POLYGONIZE
tools.description: Converts a closed chain of wires into a polygon, or a polygon back into wires. Start the command and click one of the wires, or the polygon outline. Holding Alt while clicking adds the result as a new object and keeps the original; without Alt the original is replaced.

parameters.name: Alt+click
parameters.description: Copy instead of replace.

tools.notes: Also available from the right-click menu of a wire or polygon edge as 'Convert To Polygon' / 'Convert To Wires', with the choice Copy or Replace. Related: POLYGON.

tools.name: PORT
tools.description: Adds ports to module symbols in hierarchical schematics. A port exports a net of the module (name equal to the net name inside the module) and offers a connection point for a net outside; a simple bus name exports all nets of that bus at once. Position and orientation are chosen automatically on the nearest side of the module symbol.
tools.usage:
PORT 'module_instance_name' 'net_name' options •..
PORT 'module' 'net_name' options •..
PORT 'module' 'net_name' options|DELETE

parameters.name: module_instance_name / module
parameters.description: Module instance on the sheet or module (in module context).

parameters.name: net_name
parameters.description: Net inside the module to export, or a simple bus name with one range such as 'PA[0..7]' (no aliases).

parameters.name: Direction
parameters.description: NC, In, Out, IO, OC, Hiz, Pas, Pwr; default IO. Can be changed for existing ports in module context.

parameters.name: DELETE
parameters.description: Deletes an existing port (module context).

tools.notes: The net class of the net connected to a port overrides the class of the net inside the module. Ctrl+Left selects a port at its connecting end for MOVE (along the module border), INFO and DELETE; use Ctrl+Right to cycle when a net makes the selection ambiguous. Related: MODULE.

tools.name: PREFIX
tools.description: Sets, in the device editor, the leading characters of the names that ADD generates when the device is placed in a schematic (R, C, U ...). While editing a module sheet it sets the prefix for instances of that module.

parameters.name: prefix_string
parameters.description: Prefix; parts become prefix1, prefix2, ...

tools.notes: Generated names can later be changed with NAME. Related: CONNECT, PACKAGE, VALUE, MODULE.

tools.name: PRINT
tools.description: Prints the current drawing to the system printer or to a PDF/PostScript file, using the layer colors and fill styles of the editor (always the white-background palette). A scale factor and a page limit can be given; without a terminating ';' the print dialog opens so options can be checked. Works for schematics, boards and library objects; manufacturing data comes from the CAM Processor instead.

parameters.name: factor
parameters.description: Scale factor of the output.

parameters.name: -limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of pages (the '-' distinguishes it from the factor); the factor is reduced until the drawing fits; -0 allows any number of pages so the exact factor is kept.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: MIRROR, ROTATE, UPSIDEDOWN, BLACK, SOLID, CAPTION, FILE, PRINTER, PAPER, SHEETS, ALIGN, WINDOW, PORTRAIT, LANDSCAPE, HIERARCHY (see 'PRINT options').
Prints immediately without the dialog.

tools.notes: Board polygons are printed as outlines unless RATSNEST was run first. SET DISPLAY_MODE NODRILL prints pads and vias filled without drill holes. Options given on the command line are stored in the print setup only when confirmed in the dialog (i.e. PRINT not terminated with ';').

tools.name: PRINT options
tools.description: Keywords accepted by PRINT for mirroring, rotation, colors, caption, target (printer or file), paper size, sheet range, alignment, window-only output, page orientation and hierarchical module sheets. A '-' before one of MIRROR ... CAPTION switches that option off, and a '-' alone switches all of them off.
tools.usage:
PRINT [factor] [-limit] [options] [;]
options: MIRROR ROTATE UPSIDEDOWN BLACK SOLID CAPTION FILE name PRINTER name PAPER size SHEETS range ALIGN setting WINDOW PORTRAIT LANDSCAPE HIERARCHY

parameters.name: MIRROR / ROTATE / UPSIDEDOWN
parameters.description: Mirror the output, rotate by 90 degrees, rotate by 180 degrees (with ROTATE: 270).

parameters.name: BLACK / SOLID
parameters.description: Ignore layer colors (all black) / ignore fill styles (all solid).

parameters.name: CAPTION
parameters.description: Print a caption at the bottom of the page.

parameters.name: FILE name / PRINTER name
parameters.description: Output to a file or a named printer (the last one given wins).

parameters.name: PAPER size
parameters.description: Paper name as in the dialog (A4, Letter ...) or custom WidthxHeightUnit without blanks, e.g. 200x300mm or 8.0x11.5inch; give PRINTER before PAPER.

parameters.name: SHEETS range
parameters.description: Schematic sheets from-to (2-15), a single sheet (42) or ALL; default is the current sheet.

parameters.name: ALIGN setting
parameters.description: T, C, B (vertical) and L, C, R (horizontal) in any order, e.g. TL; a single direction centers the other.

parameters.name: WINDOW
parameters.description: Print only the currently visible window area.

parameters.name: PORTRAIT / LANDSCAPE
parameters.description: Page orientation.

parameters.name: HIERARCHY
parameters.description: With SHEETS ALL, print module sheets once per module instance with the instance's part and net names.

tools.notes: If the current sheet belongs to a module, SHEETS ranges refer to that module; SHEETS ALL prints main and all module sheets. Custom paper sizes may not work with every printer and are mainly for PDF/PostScript output.

tools.name: PRINT FILE (PDF and PostScript output)
tools.description: The FILE option of PRINT writes the output to a file instead of a printer: an extension of .pdf creates a PDF (texts searchable unless they use the vector font) and .ps a PostScript file. This is the quickest way to produce PDF documentation of a schematic or board from the editor or a script.

parameters.name: file_name
parameters.description: Output file; '*' or '*.ext' opens a file dialog; only an extension (e.g. .pdf) uses the drawing's name with that extension.

parameters.name: %E / %N / %P / %%
parameters.description: Placeholders: loaded file's extension, name without path/extension, directory path, and a literal '%'. Example %N.cmp.pdf gives boardname.cmp.pdf.

tools.example:
PRINT SHEETS ALL BLACK FILE %N_schematic.pdf;
PRINT 1 -0 BLACK SOLID FILE %N.cmp.pdf;
tools.notes: A PDF can also be chosen as 'Print to File (PDF)' in the dialog's printer list. Run RATSNEST before printing a board so polygons are filled. Select the layers to print with DISPLAY beforehand.

tools.name: QROUTEAIRWIRE
tools.description: Quick Route for single airwires in the board editor: each airwire you select is routed automatically at once. Selecting an existing wire, pad or via also works when a nearby airwire can be identified unambiguously.

parameters.description: Click on the airwire (or a wire, pad or via next to it).

tools.notes: In the Design Manager, select signal or airwire entries and use right click > Quick Route to route them on the layer currently set for ROUTE. Related: QROUTESIGNAL, QROUTEMULTI, QROUTESMOOTH, ROUTE.

tools.name: QROUTESIGNAL
tools.description: Quick Route for a whole signal in the board editor: select any object of a signal (airwire, wire, pad or via) and all its airwires are routed immediately on the active layer. If the signal is one side of a differential pair, both signals are routed together.

parameters.description: Click any object of the signal.

tools.notes: Shows an error message if the signal has no airwires. Design Manager: right click > Quick Route. Related: QROUTEAIRWIRE, QROUTEMULTI.

tools.name: QROUTEMULTI
tools.description: Quick Route for several signals at once in the board editor: draw selection lines that cross the wires, pads and vias to route, add more lines as needed, then right-click to route all airwires connected to the selected objects on the active layer.

parameters.name: selection lines
parameters.description: Drawn with the mouse across the signal objects; ESC clears the selection.

parameters.name: Right click
parameters.description: Starts routing the selection.

tools.example:
QROUTEMULTI
(draw a line across the pads of the bus, right-click)
tools.notes: Design Manager: select several entries, right click > Quick Route. Related: ROUTEMULTI (interactive multi-trace routing), QROUTESIGNAL.

tools.name: QROUTESMOOTH
tools.description: Smooths an existing routed track: select a wire of a routed signal and the wire sequence on that layer is reworked to use fewer bends. Board editor.

parameters.description: Click a routed wire of the signal.

tools.notes: Related: QROUTEAIRWIRE, QROUTESIGNAL, QROUTEMULTI, MITER, OPTIMIZE.

tools.name: QUIT
tools.description: Ends the EAGLE session. If the drawing or library has unsaved changes, a prompt asks whether to save first.
tools.notes: Alt+X also exits EAGLE at any time. In scripts, save with WRITE before QUIT to avoid the save prompt. Related: CLOSE, WRITE.

tools.name: RATSNEST
tools.description: Recalculates airwires in the board editor so that unrouted connections take the shortest paths, e.g. after moving parts or after reading a netlist with SCRIPT. It also calculates all signal polygons (showing them in real mode), so pads already connected through copper get no airwires. It reports 'Ratsnest: Nothing to do!' when everything is routed, or the number of remaining airwires.

parameters.name: signal_name
parameters.description: Recalculate and show the airwires (and polygons) of these signals; wildcards * ? [...] allowed ([a-z] ranges, bracket a character to match it literally).

parameters.name: ! signal_name
parameters.description: Hide the airwires of these signals (see 'RATSNEST ! (hide airwires)').

tools.notes: RATSNEST does not mark the board as modified (polygon data is not stored). Zero-length airwires (wires of the same signal ending at one point on different layers without via, or smds on opposite sides) appear as an X in the Unrouted layer and can be routed with ROUTE or fixed with a VIA. SET POLYGON_RATSNEST OFF skips polygon calculation; the eaglerc parameter Option.RatsnestLimit limits memory for very complex signals. Differential pair airwires prefer open wire ends. Related: SIGNAL, RIPUP, POLYGON.

tools.name: RATSNEST ! (hide and show airwires)
tools.description: Hides the airwires of chosen signals, typically supply signals that will be connected by polygons and would otherwise clutter the view. Listing signals without '!' shows and recalculates them again; both forms and wildcards can be combined in one command, processed from left to right.

parameters.description: Following signal names are hidden.
Show (and recalculate) all airwires.

tools.notes: Because processing is left to right, a signal matched by both parts of the example (e.g. DGND) ends up hidden. SIGNAL makes a signal's airwires visible again when it creates a new airwire; RIPUP does not change the hidden state.

tools.name: RECT
tools.description: Draws filled rectangles given by two opposite corners; the center mouse button changes the layer. Rectangles in tRestrict, bRestrict or vRestrict define restricted areas for the Autorouter. The optional orientation is mainly for scripts generated from UL_RECTANGLE data.

parameters.name: orientation
parameters.description: R0 ... R359.9 (see ADD); S and M flags not allowed. Corner coordinates are always given for R0.

tools.notes: Rectangles in signal layers (Top, Bottom, Route2..15) do not belong to signals, so DRC reports overlaps with wires, pads etc. With a non-zero orientation entered interactively the corners may not appear at the cursor; use ROTATE to turn rectangles interactively. Related: CIRCLE, POLYGON.

tools.name: REDO
tools.description: Executes again the commands that were reverted with UNDO. The undo/redo memory reaches back to the last EDIT, OPEN or REMOVE command and is fully integrated with forward/back annotation between schematic and board.
tools.notes: UNDO LIST shows the whole buffer and allows jumping to any step. Related: UNDO, SET UNDO_LOG.

tools.name: REMOVE
tools.description: Deletes things that are addressed by name: in the board or schematic editor a file, in the library editor a device, symbol, footprint or 3D package of the open library, in a schematic a sheet, a module or a module sheet. Symbols, footprints and 3D packages can only be removed if no device (or 3D package) uses them.
tools.usage:
REMOVE name
REMOVE name.Sxx
REMOVE name.mod
REMOVE name.Mxx

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: File name (board/schematic editor) or library object name, optionally with extension (e.g. name.sym); without extension you must be in the matching edit mode.

parameters.name: .Sxx
parameters.description: Sheet number xx of the loaded schematic (name may be omitted: REMOVE .S3).

parameters.name: name.mod / name.Mxx
parameters.description: Module, or sheet xx of a module.

tools.notes: Deleting a file cannot be undone; in scripts the confirmation can be automated with SET CONFIRM YES / REMOVE filename / SET CONFIRM OFF, but use that with great care. REMOVE in a library clears the UNDO buffer. After removing the current sheet, sheet 1 is loaded and higher sheet numbers shift down by one. Related: OPEN, RENAME, MODULE.

tools.name: RENAME
tools.description: Renames a symbol, device or footprint in the open library, or a module of the current schematic. With an extension on the first name the object type is explicit; without it you must be in the matching edit mode.

parameters.name: old_name
parameters.description: Current name, optionally with extension .fpt (footprint, new in 9.1; .pac still accepted), .sym, .dev or .mod.

parameters.name: new_name
parameters.description: New name; the extension is optional here.

tools.example:
RENAME OPAMP.sym OPAMP_DUAL;
RENAME SOT23.fpt SOT23-3;
tools.notes: RENAME clears the UNDO buffer. Related: OPEN, REMOVE.

tools.name: REPLACE
tools.description: Replaces the device of a placed part with another compatible device, also from a different library; used gates and connected pins/pads must match by name or by coordinates. Without parameters a dialog lists devices of all libraries in use and every following click replaces a part. In a board without schematic (or for elements without schematic part) it replaces the footprint, controlled by SET REPLACE_SAME.
tools.usage:
REPLACE •..
REPLACE device_name[@library_name] [P3D=3d_package] •..
REPLACE part_name device_name[@library_name] [P3D=3d_package] ..
REPLACE footprint_name •..
REPLACE element_name footprint_name ..

parameters.name: device_name[@library_name]
parameters.description: New device; quote the whole term if the library name contains blanks.

parameters.name: P3D=3d_package
parameters.description: Choose the 3D package by name or URN among those of the device (not case sensitive, no wildcards).

parameters.name: part_name
parameters.description: Replace this part directly (useful in scripts).

parameters.name: footprint_name / element_name
parameters.description: Board-only mode: new footprint, optionally for a named element.

tools.example:
REPLACE R1 R-EU_R0805@rcl;
REPLACE C5 'C-EUC0603@my lib';
tools.notes: Board-only modes: SET REPLACE_SAME NAMES (default; new footprint needs the same pad/smd names, positions irrelevant) or SET REPLACE_SAME COORDS (pads at the same coordinates, names may differ); pads connected to signals must exist in the new footprint. Needs the tOrigins/bOrigins layer displayed. Replacing may trigger an automatic library update that changes other parts too: run DRC and ERC afterwards. Not allowed while an assembly variant is active. Related: UPDATE, ADD, CHANGE PACKAGE.

tools.name: RIPUP
tools.description: Turns routed wires and vias back into airwires and sets polygons back to outline display, in the board editor. It can act on all signals, on all but some, on named signals, on clicked segments (up to the next pad/smd), or with '@' on polygons only. Only objects on currently visible layers are affected.

parameters.description: Rip up all signals connected to elements (e.g. crop marks are kept).
Exclude the listed signals (RIPUP ! GND VCC;).
Act on polygons only (RIPUP @; RIPUP @ GND; RIPUP @ ! GND VCC;).

parameters.name: signal_name
parameters.description: Signals to rip up completely (only if connected to elements); wildcards * ? [...] allowed.

parameters.name: Ripup modes
parameters.description: Parameter toolbar (or SET Ripup_mode): Default/Normal, Connected Copper, Connected Copper on Same Layer, Signal, Part to Part, Ripup All Polygons, Ripup All.

tools.notes: Ctrl+Right rips up the group. Clicking an airwire converts all adjacent routed wires and vias up to the next pad, smd or airwire. Polygons ripped up by name are shown as outlines until RATSNEST. RIPUP does not change airwires hidden with RATSNEST !. Related: DELETE, GROUP, POLYGON, RATSNEST.

tools.name: ROTATE
tools.description: Changes the orientation of objects in any editor. A given orientation is added to the current one, while a leading '=' sets it absolutely. Parts, pads, smds and pins can be addressed by name, and part attributes as part>attribute (e.g. R5>VALUE).

parameters.name: orientation
parameters.description: As in ADD (e.g. R90, MR180, R45); prefix '=' for absolute (=MR90).

parameters.name: 'name'
parameters.description: Object name; the quotes distinguish it from an orientation and can be left out when unambiguous.

tools.notes: Ctrl+Right rotates the group; Left&Drag rotates an object by any angle (ESC while holding the button cancels), Ctrl+Right&Drag rotates the group around the pressed point. Locked parts cannot be rotated. Rotating an element drags connected tracks along (check for shorts) and requires tOrigins/bOrigins visible. Text stays readable from bottom or right, so its origin jumps after two rotations; use the Spin flag for upside-down text. Related: MOVE, MIRROR, LOCK, GROUP.

tools.name: ROUTE
tools.description: Interactive manual router of the board editor that turns airwires into copper wires. Start on a pad, via, wire or airwire, let the intermediate wires follow the mouse, commit each stretch with a left click and change layers on the fly (a via is placed automatically). Wire width and via come from the Design Rules and the signal's net class when 'Auto set route width and drill' is enabled.

parameters.name: width
parameters.description: Wire width in the current unit; can also be typed while routing.

parameters.name: curve | @radius
parameters.description: Draws an arc as part of the track (see LINE).

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Selects the airwire of that signal closest to the cursor; quote it if it looks like a number.

parameters.name: SWAPEND
parameters.description: Typed during routing: continue from the other end of the airwire.

tools.notes: Ambiguous start point priority: through-hole pad or current-layer smd/via, current-layer wire, airwire, other-layer smd/via, other-layer wire. Starting away from an airwire creates a new airwire to a nearby object of the same signal. Only layers entered in the Design Rules layer setup are available. Vias use the minimum layer span; a micro via is used at an smd if enabled in the Design Rules. SET SINGLE_LAYER_MODE ON greys out all other layers. See also 'ROUTE push and shove options', 'ROUTE mouse and keyboard controls' and 'ROUTE loop removal, snap and SWAPEND'. Related: ROUTEDIFF, ROUTEMULTI, QROUTE*, FANOUT, AUTO, MEANDER, RIPUP.

tools.name: ROUTE push and shove options (obstacle modes)
tools.description: Three obstacle handling modes decide what ROUTE (and ROUTEDIFF/ROUTEMULTI) does when the dragged track meets other objects: ignore them, walk around them, or push movable objects aside. Select them with the Obstacle Avoidance icons in the ROUTE parameter toolbar or with SET OBSTACLE_MODE; Walkaround is the default.

parameters.name: IGNORE
parameters.description: Wires and vias can be placed anywhere regardless of the Design Rules; you must avoid shorts yourself.

parameters.name: WALKAROUND
parameters.description: Default. Follows the Design Rules, contours around obstacles and finds the nearest legal via position on layer changes.

parameters.name: PUSH
parameters.description: Follows the Design Rules and pushes movable obstacles aside, also around a new via (push and shove routing).

tools.notes: In congested areas Walkaround and Push may not reach the cursor; a route failure indicator is then shown at the end of the track. Related: SET LOOP_REMOVAL, DRC.

tools.name: ROUTE mouse and keyboard controls
tools.description: Mouse buttons and keys used while ROUTE, ROUTEDIFF or ROUTEMULTI is active: committing segments, placing vias, cycling layers and bend styles, auto-completing and undoing commits. Knowing them makes interactive routing much faster.
tools.usage:
Left: start routing / commit segments (and via)
Shift+Left: start with the width of an existing wire / place a via and stay on the layer
Center: next routing layer (via)
Shift+Center: start layer dialog on multi-layer objects
Right: toggle left/right direction of the bend style
Shift+Right / Ctrl+Right: previous / next bend style (SET WIRE_BEND)
Enter: commit and auto-complete to the airwire target
Space / Shift+Space: next / previous routing layer (via)
Backspace (Delete on macOS): undo the last left-click commit
Ctrl+Space / Ctrl+Shift+Space: cycle the start layer forward / backward

parameters.name: Enter
parameters.description: Commits the cursor position and completes the route to the airwire's anchor object.

parameters.name: Backspace
parameters.description: Unwinds commits one by one, including vias and layer changes; only works when the command line is empty.

parameters.name: Shift+Left
parameters.description: Force a via without changing the layer.

tools.example: ROUTE, click the pad, move, left-click to commit, press Space to go to the next layer (via follows the cursor), left-click to place the via, press Enter to finish to the target pad.
tools.notes: The initial layer is the current layer if a start object exists there, otherwise the layer of the object at the start point. Width can be typed at any time and also sizes the via. Related: SET WIRE_BEND, MITER.

tools.name: ROUTE loop removal, snap and SWAPEND
tools.description: Loop removal lets you re-route part of an existing track between two pads and deletes the now redundant old wires (and vias) automatically; it is on by default. The snap function pulls the cursor onto a same-signal target object within SNAP_LENGTH, independent of the grid, and marks it with an X. SWAPEND jumps to the opposite end of the airwire being routed, panning the view if needed.

parameters.name: LOOP_REMOVAL
parameters.description: ON (default) / OFF; also available as parameter toolbar buttons.

parameters.name: SNAP_LENGTH distance
parameters.description: Snap radius in the current grid unit (default 20 mil).

parameters.name: SWAPEND
parameters.description: Typed into the command line while routing, or assigned to a key with ASSIGN.

tools.notes: Loop removal fails if the loop contains a component pad or the existing wires form a T-junction; re-routes can start and end at pads, vias, wire vertices or mid-wire. ROUTEDIFF and ROUTEMULTI do not implement loop removal. Backspace does not undo a SWAPEND.

tools.name: ROUTEDIFF
tools.description: Differential-pair router of the board editor: it highlights all differential pairs, and clicking an airwire or copper of one pair routes both signals in parallel with the gap, wire widths and via sizes of their net class. Otherwise it works like ROUTE (same mouse and key controls) except that loop removal is not available.

parameters.name: Pair naming
parameters.description: Two signals with the same name ending in _P and _N (e.g. CLOCK_P, CLOCK_N) in the same net class.

parameters.name: SwapEnd
parameters.description: Command-line input: continue from the opposite airwire end.

tools.notes: Widths and gap come from the net class regardless of 'Auto set route width and drill'. At the start, where the pair is not yet at the required distance, wires run from the start points to the cursor following the bend style. Finish with Enter (QuickRoute completion) or by moving over copper at the opposite end; if that fails, finish each leg with ROUTE. Balance lengths with MEANDER. Related: CLASS, QROUTESIGNAL.

tools.name: ROUTEMULTI
tools.description: Routes several airwires at the same time as a bundle in the board editor. Draw selection lines through the wires, pads and vias to include (more lines add more signals, ESC clears), right-click to start, then route like with ROUTE; the wires keep a controllable spacing and vias are placed in a chosen pattern on layer changes.

parameters.name: DecSpacing / IncSpacing
parameters.description: Command-line keywords: decrease / increase the spacing between the wires by the grid distance.

parameters.name: MinSpacing
parameters.description: Set the spacing to the minimum allowed by the design rules.

parameters.name: SwapEnd
parameters.description: Continue from the opposite airwire end points.

parameters.name: SET VIA_PATTERN
parameters.description: PERPENDICULAR (default), ANGLE_LEFT, ANGLE_RIGHT or STAGGER placement of the vias on a layer change.

tools.example:
SET VIA_PATTERN STAGGER;
ROUTEMULTI
(draw a selection line across the bus pads, right-click, route)
MinSpacing
tools.notes: Initial spacing equals the spacing of the start objects. Spacing keywords and via patterns can be typed, chosen in the parameter toolbar or assigned to keys with ASSIGN. Loop removal is not implemented. Mouse/key controls are the same as for ROUTE. Related: QROUTEMULTI, ROUTE, FANOUT.
